sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the interactive Fuzzy String Distance Studio. Try typing variations or test presets like Martha versus Marhta and Smith versus Smythe to observe real-time Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, and Soundex responses.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Notice how Soundex groups Smith and Smythe into the exact same blocking code S530, while Levenshtein drops to 66% on Marhta due to transposition!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Checkpoint 1: Given CRANE versus TRANE and CRANE versus CRATE, both sharing 4 letters with zero transpositions, calculate how the three-character common prefix CRA changes the Winkler score.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Both have a base Jaro score of 0.8667, but the three-letter prefix CRA gives CRATE a Winkler bonus of 0.0400, boosting it to 0.9067!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding derivation! The common prefix CRA of length 3 with scaling factor 0.1 boosts Jaro-Winkler similarity from 0.8667 up to 0.9067, while CRANE versus TRANE has zero prefix bonus.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect calculation. With common prefix length 3, Winkler scaling adds 3 times 0.1 times 1 minus 0.8667, which equals 0.0400. Adding this to 0.8667 yields 0.9067.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Fellegi-Sunter and Search Compression Workbench. In Tab 1, toggle attribute agreements to observe log-odds bit weights and Neyman-Pearson triage. In Tab 2, adjust database size and bucket count to verify search reduction.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at Tab 1: when postal code disagrees, the weight drops by only 2.7 bits, so the pair remains in Auto-Merge because name and birthdate provide over 13 bits of evidence!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Checkpoint 2: For 100,000 records partitioned into 500 blocks of 200 records each, calculate the surviving candidate pairs and explain why rare surnames generate higher bit weights than gender.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Blocking reduces 5 billion pairs down to 9.95 million, cutting 99.8% of the search space. And rare names like Zephyros have minuscule coincidence probabilities, yielding over 16 bits of evidence!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Brilliant mastery! Partitioning into 500 blocks eliminates 99.80% of pairwise comparisons, and because match weights scale inversely with coincidence probability, rare surnames yield massive positive bit scores.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Blocking reduces brute-force pairs from 5 billion to 9.95 million, which is a 99.80% elimination. Furthermore, match weights scale inversely with coincidence probability u sub k.
